title: Buyer-Observed Model Behavior Mapping + Claims Audit
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a buyer-centric map that links observed model behaviors (latency, hallucination modes, formatting consistency, safety filters) to vendor claims and measurable product impact for enterprise procurement teams.

Scope: 1) Sample ~10 commercial and open models across short/long context usage patterns (search, summarization, RAG, code-completion). 2) Run curated customer-style prompts (derived from 6 enterprise buyer interviews) to surface divergence between vendor marketing claims and measurable behavior. 3) Produce a prioritized list of claim discrepancies with estimated impact on adoption and rollout risk.

Success criteria: deliver a reproducible evaluation sheet, triaged discrepancy list (High/Medium/Low impact), a one-page executive brief for Sales/PS, and a set of tactical recommendations for Console/Docs (e.g., explicit guidance on model selection for low-latency vs high-fidelity workflows).
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible evaluation workbook with inputs and seeds
Top-10 claim discrepancies with evidence links
Executive brief summarizing 3 buyer-facing guidance items
At least one follow-up experiment ticket created for runtime team
comments: 2025-02-12 Liam Chen: Kickoff - interviewed 6 buyers from FinServ and RegTech verticals. Consolidated buyer pain into three probes: hallucination in regulatory summarization, embedding drift in long-lived indices, and time-to-first-byte latency objections. Created initial prompt set in spreadsheet.

2025-02-15 Priya Nair (Research): Ran baseline evaluation across 8 model variants. Early signal: one vendor's 'deterministic formatting' claim fails on multi-turn invoice parsing 27% of the time. Added raw outputs to sheet.

2025-02-17 Marco Ruiz (Sales): Flagged a top customer who was promised 'sub-200ms median' for short completions — we should surface that discrepancy as a sales-ready talking point. Linking to customer thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1616161616

2025-02-18 Aisha Kapoor: Design reviewed executive brief draft; suggested highlighting fallback strategies (model variant pinning, structured output enforcement) as mitigation. Requesting a short rerun focused on model-mix routing scenarios.

2025-02-20 Riley Park (Runtime): Noted blocker — quantized model build for dedicated pool hits OOM on sequence length >2048 in our current infra image. Created dependency ENG-18877 to track memory/quant kernel tuning. Suggested temporary limit in our experiment runner until kernel fix lands.
notes: Runbook: use spreadsheet tabs to separate raw outputs, normalized metrics (latency P50/P95, hallucination rate, formatting fidelity), and vendor-claim crosswalk.
Edge case: anonymize any customer-owned prompts before saving outputs to company docs (legal signoff in Confluence).
Recommendation: create a short 'Model Claim Verification' badge we can surface in model catalog if discrepancies are low-risk.
